title: A shell around the board
summary: React takes ownership of Home, Match, Replay and Profile. Phaser becomes the board renderer.

title: A flatter, quieter game
summary: Fewer nested frames, clearer button roles and ledger-like history rows. Undo and replay branching join the play loop.

title: Mobile gets its own layout
summary: Intentional portrait compositions, touch placement and a shared pixel icon language.

title: The local-play baseline
summary: Tighter rails, quieter labels and safer short-screen flow complete the first local product.

title: An optional cloud identity
summary: Profile gains Google sign-in and explicit local, loading, signed-in and unavailable states.

title: Continuity after sign-in
summary: Local identity and games can move into private cloud state, with visible import progress.

title: One private history
summary: Signed-in history, sync recovery and an inline reset flow become part of the record screen.

title: Keep the record compact
summary: Small sync badges, Show more history and explicit cloud deletion complete the account controls.

title: The lab becomes visible
summary: Published rankings, match trees and search metrics give bot experiments a browsable surface.

title: Read the bot comparison
summary: Ranking rows, pairwise expansion and mobile report navigation become easier to inspect.

title: Explain a finished game
summary: Analysis reports add proof boards, threat hints and per-turn explanations beside cleaner bot comparisons.

title: Settings gets a home
summary: Game and bot controls leave Profile. Presets, advanced settings, hints and timers become player-facing.

title: Replay becomes analysis
summary: The replay page gains progressive analysis, timeline marks and a shared board-overlay vocabulary.

title: Find the turning point
summary: The timeline separates setup, lethal onset and the last escape; status language follows the current frame.

title: Make the evidence readable
summary: Mistake-aware status, configurable evidence and calmer markers explain why the game turned.

title: Bring the tools into the product
summary: Lab and Visuals become first-class app pages with the game's shared presentation.

title: Teach from inside the game
summary: Rules and Guide join the navigation, using actual board-rendered examples and clearer analysis entry points.

title: A more usable baseline
summary: Keyboard play, clearer controls and recovery, reduced motion and refined mobile teaching pages.

title: Games can travel
summary: Portable replay links, saved study copies and public player records add explicit sharing flows.

title: A public page with a useful record
summary: Two-column identity and record, compact games, and consistent mobile actions make sharing easier to explore.
